## Bayesian Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine: Volume I: Bayesian Clinical Trials

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 12 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or computed), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.0.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Clinical Trials and Personalized Medicine: Volume I: Bayesian Clinical Trials](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova, Vadim Sokolov and Nicholas G. Polson (2026). Volume I of a two volume series. Bayesian clinical trials built up from the traditional trial and tied to regulation: calibration, monitoring, safety, borrowing, adaptive designs, and reanalyses of landmark trials, with an R package and an online lab. Keywords: Bayesian clinical trials, adaptive trial design, group sequential design, interim monitoring, type I error calibration, FDA Bayesian guidance, multiplicity and shrinkage, informative priors, e-values, operating characteristics simulation, biostatistics, R package.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24122876): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24122876 for version 1.0.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24122875 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page

- [Main result: The three deviation scales (evidence tolls)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#evidence_tolls_three_scales): Section 11.9.2, page 249, proved. A fixed level test, a Bayes rule and an anytime valid rule act at three different sizes of the squared standardized score; for the normal mixture the anytime valid bar exceeds the Bayes bar by a surcharge that is about 2 log(1/alpha) at large information.
- [Main result: The surcharge for validity at every stopping time is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial requirement, as a comparison of boundary terms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#surcharge_seventy_percent): Section 11.9.4, page 252, proved. For the normal mixture e value rule, against the uncalibrated Bayes factor bar (posterior odds of one), the large information surcharge 7.38 is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial standardized requirement 10.51; this compares boundary terms and is not an exact sample size identity.
- [Main result: Moderate deviation sample size equation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#moderate_deviation_sample_size): Section 9.3.2, page 198, proved. A Bayes rule whose bar grows like the logarithm of the sample size has an implicit sample size equation, the textbook formula with the critical value replaced by the square root of log n plus a constant.
- [Main result: Calibration of a posterior probability rule by the null maximum](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#null_maximum_calibration): Section 14.4.1, page 305, proved. The smallest threshold that holds a monitored posterior probability rule to level alpha is the (1 minus alpha) quantile of the largest posterior probability reached over the looks in null simulations, so one simulation serves every threshold.
- [Main result: Exact backward induction for binary endpoints on a cubic lattice](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#backward_induction_states): Section 15.6.2, page 338, proved. For a two arm binary trial the Bayes optimal stopping rule depends only on the success counts and the stage, so backward induction is exact on a lattice of order T cubed states.
- [Main result: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 21.1.2, page 472, computed. In our reconstruction of SELECT at hazard ratio 0.80, a calibrated Bayesian rule stops at a median of 464 events among trials that declare efficacy and 486 over all trials, against 817 for SELECT's planned design (one interim analysis with Lan-DeMets spending, then the final); the e value rule and a four look design are slower or less powerful.
- [Main result: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.12.1, page 132, computed. The statistical analysis plan's beta binomial model with a Beta(0.700102, 1) prior, applied to 8 versus 162 cases, gives a posterior probability that vaccine efficacy exceeds 30 per cent of 1 minus 2e-28 and a point estimate of 95 per cent, matching the published interval within a tenth of a point.
- [Computed: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.12.1, page 132
- [Computed: The Bayes factor bar exceeds the fixed level bar once information times prior variance passes about 46](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#bayes_bar_crossing_46): Section 7.5.1, page 144
- [Computed: Moderate deviation and textbook sizes at the SELECT hazard ratio of 0.80 (not a prediction of SELECT's size)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#moderate_deviation_select_comparison): Section 9.3.6, page 203
- [Computed: Four operation ulcer example, adjusted p value against posterior probability](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#ulcer_bonferroni_vs_posterior): Section 10.5.3, page 228
- [Computed: A utility only backward induction rule declares treatment better half the time under the null](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#utility_only_rule_null_declaration): Section 15.6.3, page 341
- [Computed: Shared control false positive counts for four arms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#shared_control_false_positive_counts): Section 20.4.1, page 448
- [Computed: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials_v1/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 21.1.2, page 472
